newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's MAAF interested in GAN - paper.
newsitem.headline: France's MAAF interested in GAN - paper.

text.p: The head of French mutual insurer MAAF said on Friday in a newspaper interview the company might be interested in teaming up with other companies to buy state-owned insurer GAN.

"With our current size, all of GAN would be too big a chunk but we could be a candidate to buy it if we teamed up with others," MAAF chairman Jean-Claude Seys was quoted by business daily L'Agefi as saying.
Seys said he had already received expressions of interest from foreign companies. "The contacts we have had...prove we could manage the financing without problem," he said.
He added the strategic value of GAN could be higher than its book value and that it might be more profitable for the state to sell off GAN business by business.
The previous conservative government had promised the European Commission that GAN would be privatised in exchange for the Commission's approval of a 20 billion-franc aid package for GAN.

But the new Socialist government, which campaigned on an anti-privatisation platform, put the sale on hold. However, it is believed it will proceed with the sale to meet Commission requirements for approval of the rescue plan.
French insurer AGF has shown strong interest in GAN's insurance operations to build up its presence in the sector following last year's mega-merger of AXA and Union des Assurances de Paris.
There are also potential foreign suitors including Germany's Allianz and Belgium's Fortis
